evidence: The track starts at Ferry Landing Wharf.
Follow the track as it leads along the edge of the harbour then climbs to the remains of a well-fortified Ngāti Hei pā site.
The track continues along top of the Whitianga Rock peninsula, with dramatic views of Whitianga Harbour and Back Bay.

evidence: You can combine Whitianga Rock Walk and Maramaratotoara Track to form a loop.

Starting from Ferry Landing Wharf, follow Whitianga Rock Walk to the pā site, then turn off onto Maramaratotoara Track. Continue on Maramaratotoara Track to Maramaratotoara Bay, the follow the footpath back to Ferry Landing Wharf.

The track then climbs to the historic pā site, where it connects with Whitianga Rock Walk.

doubts: The page covers two tracks plus a loop; W1 (Whitianga Rock Walk) is taken as main because DOC's '20 min return' fits its 300 m one way, but the page could also be read as a network. The text does not name where Whitianga Rock Walk ends; it is taken as the top/end of the Whitianga Rock peninsula, returning the same way (not stated explicitly). Ferry Landing Wharf is taken as road end F2 (the western Purangi Road end, nearer Ferry Landing) and Maramaratotara Bay start as F3 (the eastern one, nearer Maramaratotara Bay); both features carry the same name. Maramaratotara Track's '1 km one way' does not say whether it is walked back, so its shape is left null.
